newsitem.title: UK: Russian gold sector hopes for gold exchange-banker.
newsitem.headline: Russian gold sector hopes for gold exchange-banker.

text.p: Russia's cash-strapped gold mining industry hopes to see a gold exchange open in Moscow in coming months, a Russian banker with close ties to the industry said on Monday.

An exchange modelled on Western gold markets would give Russia a spot and futures market and help the industry to raise badly needed capital, said Lev Weinberg, head of BamCredit bank, whose gold producing clients have a combined output of 30 tonnes per year.

Russia's tightly controlled gold sector has felt the pain of the country's economic crisis over the past year. Cheap credits have come to an end and the centralised purchasing and exporting agencies have delayed payments to producers for months, he said.
"Currently noone can pay for the gold that's being produced...It's terrible. People go without being paid for two or three months," Weinberg told journalists.
"If we do not set up an exchange in the first half of 1997, Russian gold output will decrease catastrophically."

Some 45 tonnes of gold had been stockpiled by refiners and producers, because miners were not being paid for their output, he added. The Soviet Union in its heyday produced up to 300 tonnes of gold per year. Russia now produces only some 120 tonnes.
Weinberg and officials of Russia's industry and finance ministries were in London for fact-finding meetings with banks including the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development.
Government approval for the gold exchange has yet to be clinched, with sticky regulations governing the export of physical gold a critical element, Weinberg said.
Eight banks have nominal rights to export gold, but very little of it leaves the country because of heavy red tape.
But Weinberg said the government was warming to the idea of letting go of some export controls in the face of plummeting output.
The exchange would also tap the domestic market, which he said could support a maximum of 30 tonnes annually.
"When we offered gold coins to Russians, they were snapped up," Weinberg said.

The members of the exchange would be small banks and structures dealing with the gold industry. The players on the exchange would be the government, along with large banks -- Russian and Western -- and gold proudcers.
